newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails Yeltsin's rejection of religion law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails Yeltsin's rejection of religion law.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday hailed Russian President Boris Yeltsin's veto of a draft law curbing religious freedom, calling it a victory for Russian democracy.
"We welcome President Yeltsin's decision to reject this legislation and his continuing support for freedom of religion," said State Department spokesman James Foley.
"In our view it is a victory for Russian democracy and religious freedom," Foley told reporters.

The bill, approved by Russia's parliament but strongly opposed by the United States and the Vatican, identified Orthodoxy, Islam, Buddhism and Judaism as traditional faiths in Russia. Representatives of other faiths, including Catholicism, feared they could lose their legal rights.
"President Yeltsin's action reaffirms Russia's commitment to fostering an open and tolerant society, in which freedom of conscience and assembly are inalienable rights," Foley said.
He said Washington hoped that any amended version of the law would promote religious freedom and tolerance in Russia.
Yeltsin rejected the law on Tuesday, the same day that the State Department issued a report on religious freedom around the world that contained criticism of the Russian draft legislation.
President Bill Clinton had raised U.S. concerns over the law directly with Yeltsin at a Group of Seven summit in Denver, Colorado, last month.
